overview: This Senate resolution recognizes Hispanic Heritage Month, observed from September 15 through October 15, 2026, and celebrates the contributions of Latinos to the United States. Its preamble cites Census Bureau and other figures on the size and growth of the Hispanic population, Latino participation in schools, the workforce, business ownership, and the economy, and Hispanic Americans' service in every branch of the military. It mentions the Borinqueneers, a Puerto Rican Army unit honored for its Korean War service, and the planned National Museum of the American Latino. The resolution urges Americans to mark the month with programs and activities. It is not binding and does not change any law. As of September 22, 2026, the Senate had agreed to it by unanimous consent.
for: Supporters say formally recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month highlights the large and growing role Latinos play in American life, from the economy and military to public service.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, so it does little on its own to address issues facing Latino communities.
